title: [finding] the `agent.tools` retirement's author-facing citation is ADR-0064 — Proposed, cloud-owned and part-superseded — while ADR-0109 (Accepted, implemented) is what the release notes lead with
body:
Filed by the `domain:cli` execution PM seat (session `session_015QE8qk46e5CHJxyQEUjbf8`, seat post #6024) out of the `os explain` catalog family (#15170–#15176 / PR #16924). Surfaced by that PR's delivering seat as a conflict it declined to chase inside a catalog PR; re-measured here before filing.

⛔ **Not graded, not routed, no `domain:*` label, no assignee — that is triage's.** ⛔ And ⛔ **nothing here re-opens the retirement itself**: `agent.tools` is retired, the rejection is correct, and the behaviour is not in question. This card is about **which decision the author is pointed at**.

## The three ADRs, read at `origin/main@9a89a0040d`

| ADR | title | status line, verbatim |
|:--|:--|:--|
| **ADR-0064** | Tool scoping — an agent's tools are exactly its skills' tools | ⚠️ **Proposed** (2026-06-22) — **cloud-owned** (2026-07-16 audit): *"the tool-resolution scoping, global fall-through removal, and bind-time affinity error live in cloud `service-ai` and are not verifiable in this repo."* Its header additionally carries **🔶 Cloud-owned — superseded in part by cloud ADR-0025 (2026-06-25)** |
| **ADR-0109** | The AI tool authoring model — the default third-party path needs no tool records | ⭐ **Accepted — implemented (Phase 1)** (2026-07-28), with in-repo evidence named in the status block (`platform-tool-names.ts`, `validate-ai-tool-references.ts` wired into `REFERENCE_INTEGRITY_RULES`). *Builds on* ADR-0064 |
| ADR-0106 | metadata-plane FLS object-schema masking | Accepted — ⛔ **unrelated**; it appears here only because it was mis-cited for this fact in a dispatch word and two triage comments (corrected on #15170, `5588724679`) |

## The asymmetry

**The author sees ADR-0064.** `packages/spec/src/ai/agent.zod.ts:237` builds the rejection message with *"(ADR-0064), so move each reference into a skill: a platform tool by its …"*. `packages/spec/src/conversions/registry.ts:786` says the same: *"agent key 'tools' removed — declare capability in a skill (ADR-0064, #3894)"*. The pin at `packages/spec/src/ai/agent.test.ts:69` is titled *"agent.tools retirement (ADR-0064 / #3820, tombstoned in #3894)"*.

**The release notes lead with ADR-0109.** `content/docs/releases/v17.mdx:719` — *"`agent.tools[]` is removed — capability comes from skills (**ADR-0109**, #3820)"* — and only then explains the invariant *via* ADR-0064 at `:721`.

⇒ One enforced retirement, two citations, and **the one an author receives at the moment of failure is the weaker of the two**: Proposed rather than Accepted, cloud-owned rather than in-repo, and marked part-superseded by a cloud ADR this repo cannot open.

## Reach — measured, so nobody re-derives it

`ADR-0064` is cited in **12 files** across `content/docs`, `docs/adr` and `docs/audits`, in addition to the three `packages/spec` sites above:

```
content/docs/ai/agents.mdx                    4
content/docs/ai/tools.mdx                     2
content/docs/getting-started/common-patterns.mdx  1
content/docs/references/ai/agent.mdx          1
content/docs/releases/v17.mdx                 1
docs/adr/0063-…                               4
docs/adr/0064-…                               1
docs/adr/0080-…                               1
docs/adr/0084-…                               1
docs/adr/0109-…                               1
docs/adr/PRIORITIZATION.md                    1
docs/audits/2026-06-ask-build-agent-development-assessment.md  7
```

⚠️ **A count is not a work list.** Some of those are legitimately about ADR-0064 *as a design record* (ADR-0109's own `Builds on` line, the audit) and must not be retargeted. ⛔ This is not a `sed` job — #11501 drew exactly that line for a different retarget (*"a classification pass, not a sed"*) and it applies here.

## Precedent, so this is filed as an instance rather than as news

⭐ **#5063** (closed) is the identical defect class one ADR over: *「ADR-0076 的状态行仍是 `Proposed`，但它已被 AGENTS.md、runtime 代码注释与多个在飞 issue 当作生效决定引用」*. ⭐ **#11501** (closed) is the remedy shape: retargeting general-rule citations from one ADR to another as a classification pass. Whoever takes this should read both before choosing an approach.

## What a fix has to answer first — ⛔ not answered here

The two obvious routes are not equivalent and neither is mine to pick:

1. **Retarget the author-facing citations to ADR-0109**, leaving design-record references to ADR-0064 intact — the #11501 shape, and consistent with what the release notes already do.
2. **Move ADR-0064's status** to reflect that the framework half is in fact enforced in this repo, or record on it which half is. ⚠️ That is an ADR status change and touches a **cloud-owned** record — the maintainer's floor, ⛔ not a lane decision.

⚠️ There is a third possibility that should be checked before either: the two ADRs may be citing **different halves** of one fact — ADR-0064 the invariant (*an agent's tool set is its skills' tools*) and ADR-0109 the authoring model that made it real — in which case the rejection message quoting the invariant's ADR is defensible and the fix is one clarifying clause, not a retarget. ⛔ Not measured here.

## Dedupe — method stated

`search_issues` over this repo for the ADR-citation family returned **9** results with the positive control firing (the class is real and populated: #5063, #11501, #7866, #12867 all came back). **None is this instance** — no open or closed card names ADR-0064's status against the `agent.tools` rejection. Nearest neighbours are #5063 (same class, ADR-0076) and #11501 (same remedy shape, ADR-0057→ADR-0124), both closed.

## Why it was not folded into PR #16924

That PR is the `os explain` catalog (`packages/cli`), and the citation lives in `packages/spec` plus a dozen docs pages. The delivering seat carried the zod message's own number into the catalog so that an author who hits the rejection and then runs `os explain agent` sees **one** number rather than two — ⭐ the right call for that PR, and the reason this is a separate card rather than a rider on it.
